item.title: Fire erupts at Havana refinery as Cuba endures US oil blockade
item.description:
A fire erupted Friday at the Ñico López refinery in Havana Bay, dealing another blow to Cuba as the island nation struggles with an intensifying energy crisis caused by a U.S.-imposed oil blockade. Dense black smoke was seen rising from the facility, though authorities have not confirmed casualties or damage to oil storage tanks.

The blaze comes as Cuba has gone a full month without a major fuel delivery, according to data analytics firm Kpler cited by Bloomberg. Since the Trump administration's January 29 executive order threatening tariffs on any nation supplying oil to Cuba, the island's two primary suppliers—Venezuela and Mexico—have halted shipments, leaving the country's aging power infrastructure starved of the roughly 100,000 barrels of crude it needs daily.

item.title: Trump sends second carrier to Gulf as Iran fortifies nuclear site
item.description: Iran is reinforcing tunnel entrances at a major underground complex near its Natanz nuclear facility, according to new satellite imagery analyzed by the Institute for Science and International Security (ISIS), a U.S.-based think tank. The developments come as the Trump administration deploys additional military assets to the Middle East and nuclear negotiations between Washington and Tehran hang in the balance.

item.title: Zelensky says Ukraine won't hold referendum on 'bad' peace deal
item.description:
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky offered a detailed account of his approach to peace negotiations with Russia in an exclusive interview with The Atlantic, published Thursday as he prepared to attend the Munich Security Conference. Speaking with journalist Simon Shuster, Zelensky emphasized Ukraine's willingness to engage constructively with U.S.-led proposals while setting firm conditions for any final agreement.

"The tactic we chose is for the Americans not to think that we want to continue the war," Zelensky told The Atlantic. "That's why we started supporting their proposals in any format that speeds things along."

item.title: Blue Origin reveals accelerated Moon plan as SpaceX pivots from Mars
item.description:
The race to return humans to the lunar surface has entered a new phase this week, with both SpaceX and Blue Origin unveiling aggressive strategies to beat China to the Moon, while Beijing continues to make steady progress toward its 2030 landing goal.

On February 9, Elon Musk announced a dramatic shift in SpaceX's priorities, revealing that the company has pivoted toward building a "self-growing city" on the Moon within the next decade. The announcement, made on his social media platform X, marks a stark reversal for the billionaire, who as recently as last year dismissed lunar missions as a "distraction" from his Mars ambitions. According to Reuters, Musk said traveling to Mars is only possible every 26 months, while launches to the Moon can occur every 10 days, allowing SpaceX to "iterate much faster."

item.title: Cornell study pinpoints global crop emissions to 10-kilometer resolution
item.description:
Researchers have produced the most comprehensive map of global cropland greenhouse gas emissions to date, revealing that just four crops—rice, maize, oil palm, and wheat—account for nearly three-quarters of all emissions from farming, with rice alone responsible for 43%.

The study, published February 13 in Nature Climate Change, synthesizes data from ground measurements, remote sensing, inventory surveys, and hydrological models to achieve a spatial resolution of approximately 10 kilometers—enabling emissions to be pinpointed not just by country, but by individual crops and management practices.

item.title: NASA extracts oxygen from lunar soil using solar energy
item.description:
NASA has achieved a milestone in lunar resource utilization, completing integrated prototype testing that used concentrated solar energy to extract oxygen from simulated lunar soil. The Carbothermal Reduction Demonstration project, known as CaRD, confirmed the production of carbon monoxide through a solar-driven chemical reaction, marking a key advance toward sustaining human exploration on the Moon.

The successful test represents a step toward enabling astronauts to produce propellant using only lunar materials and sunlight, which could reduce the cost and complexity of maintaining a long-term presence on the lunar surface. The same technology could eventually be adapted to convert carbon dioxide into oxygen and methane on Mars.

item.title: SpaceX Crew-12 to dock with ISS on Valentine's Day
item.description:
A SpaceX Falcon 9 rocket lifted off early Friday morning carrying four astronauts toward the International Space Station, marking the 12th operational crew rotation mission under NASA's Commercial Crew Program. The Crew Dragon capsule "Freedom" is set to dock with the orbiting outpost this afternoon, delivering a relief crew after an unprecedented medical evacuation last month left the station short-staffed.

The mission launched at 5:15 a.m. EST on February 13 from Space Launch Complex 40 at Cape Canaveral Space Force Station in Florida. The crew consists of NASA astronauts Jessica Meir, serving as commander, and Jack Hathaway as pilot, along with mission specialists Sophie Adenot of the European Space Agency and Andrey Fedyaev of Roscosmos.

item.title: NASA reviews Artemis II test data as moon mission eyes March
item.description:
NASA engineers are analyzing data from a confidence test conducted on February 12 as the agency works toward returning humans to the Moon for the first time in more than five decades. The test was designed to evaluate repairs made following a hydrogen leak that forced NASA to push back the Artemis II launch from its original February window.

During the test at Kennedy Space Center, operators partially filled the Space Launch System core stage liquid hydrogen tank to assess newly replaced seals in the propellant fueling area, NASA said in a statement. Teams encountered an issue with ground support equipment that reduced the flow of liquid hydrogen into the rocket, though engineers were able to achieve several key objectives and collect data at the same point in testing where a leak had been detected during the previous wet dress rehearsal.

item.title: Iran arrests over 50,000 in dragnet after deadly protest crackdown
item.description:
Iranian security forces have arrested more than 50,000 people in a sweeping campaign following a brutal crackdown last month that killed thousands of demonstrators, according to human rights groups. The dragnet, spanning major cities and rural towns, has targeted protesters, doctors, lawyers, students, actors, and reformist political figures, with many held incommunicado for days or weeks.

The Associated Press reported that security agents have conducted late-night raids on homes and workplaces across the country, using surveillance footage and facial recognition technology to track down individuals who participated in protests that peaked in early January.

item.title: Rubio urges transatlantic unity as Europe stresses self-reliance
item.description:
The 62nd Munich Security Conference opened this weekend to a fractured Western alliance, with European leaders delivering pointed assessments of transatlantic relations while U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio attempted to reassure anxious allies that Washington still values its oldest partnerships.

German Chancellor Friedrich Merz set the tone on Friday when he declared that the rules-based world order "no longer exists" and acknowledged that "a deep divide has opened between Europe and the United States." Speaking directly to the American delegation, Merz warned that U.S. claims to global leadership have been "challenged, and possibly lost," while urging Europe to stop denying the scale of the geopolitical challenge it faces.

item.title: UK and allies say Navalny was killed with rare dart frog toxin
item.description:
Russian opposition leader Alexei Navalny was poisoned with epibatidine, a lethal toxin found in South American poison dart frogs, according to a joint announcement by five European nations on the second anniversary of his death in a Siberian penal colony.

The United Kingdom, France, Germany, Sweden, and the Netherlands issued a joint statement on Saturday confirming that analyses of samples from Navalny "conclusively confirmed the presence of epibatidine," a substance not found naturally in Russia. The announcement, made at the Munich Security Conference, directly implicates the Russian government in Navalny's death, with the coalition stating that "only the Russian state had the combined means, motive and disregard for international law" to carry out the attack.

item.title: SpaceX Crew-12 docks at ISS after medical evacuation cut short previous mission
item.description:
Four astronauts aboard NASA's SpaceX Crew-12 mission docked at the International Space Station on Saturday, bringing the orbital laboratory back to its full seven-person complement following an unprecedented medical evacuation that cut short the previous crew's stay.

The Dragon spacecraft Freedom linked up with the station's Harmony module at approximately 3:15 p.m. EST, capping a 34-hour journey that began with a predawn launch from Cape Canaveral Space Force Station on Friday. The mission marks NASA's twelfth operational crew rotation under its Commercial Crew Program with SpaceX.

item.title: Russia investigates tanker crash at key Baltic oil port
item.description:
Russian authorities on Sunday launched an investigation into an incident involving an oil tanker at the Ust-Luga seaport, a key outlet for the nation's crude oil and fuel exports via the Baltic Sea. The collision, which occurred on Saturday, damaged port infrastructure but resulted in no injuries or petroleum spills.

According to the Northwestern Transport Prosecutor, the tanker Tony struck a berth wall while arriving at the port in the Leningrad region to load petroleum products. The collision damaged both the berth wall and a port crane at the facility, Reuters reported.

"The incident damaged the berth wall and the port crane. There were no injuries, and no petroleum spill occurred," the prosecutor said in a statement posted on Telegram.

item.title: Trump says Board of Peace nations pledge $5B for Gaza
item.description:
President Donald Trump said Sunday that member states of his Board of Peace have pledged more than $5 billion for humanitarian and reconstruction efforts in Gaza, while also committing thousands of personnel to a UN-authorized stabilization force in the Palestinian territory.

The announcement, made via Truth Social, comes ahead of the first formal gathering of the Board of Peace, scheduled for February 19 at the Donald J. Trump Institute of Peace in Washington, D.C.. Trump emphasized that Hamas must uphold its "commitment to full and immediate demilitarization" as part of the US-brokered ceasefire agreement.

item.title: Ukrainian drone strike hits Russian Black Sea port before Geneva talks
item.description:
A Ukrainian drone strike set fires at Russia's Taman port in the Krasnodar region on Sunday, wounding two people and damaging oil infrastructure, as both sides prepare for US-brokered peace talks scheduled for this week in Geneva. The attack comes amid intensified diplomatic maneuvering and continued fighting ahead of the fourth anniversary of Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine on February 24.

Krasnodar Governor Veniamin Kondratyev said an oil storage tank, warehouse, and terminals sustained damage in the village of Volna, where Taman port is located. More than 100 personnel were working to extinguish multiple fires at the site, he said in a Telegram post. Ukraine's military intelligence confirmed the overnight strike on the oil terminal.

item.title: Trump pledged support for Israeli strikes on Iran if talks fail
item.description:
President Donald Trump told Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu during their December meeting at Mar-a-Lago that the United States would support Israeli strikes on Iran's ballistic missile program if Washington's negotiations with Tehran collapse, according to CBS News, citing two sources familiar with the matter.

The disclosure comes as a second round of nuclear talks between the U.S. and Iran is set to begin in Geneva next week, with a U.S. delegation including envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner scheduled to meet with Iranian officials on Tuesday.

item.title: Satellite images reveal China expanding nuclear sites in Sichuan
item.description:
Satellite imagery has revealed rapid expansion at Chinese nuclear weapons facilities in Sichuan Province, signaling an accelerating effort to modernize Beijing's arsenal as global arms control frameworks weaken.

The images, first reported by The New York Times on Saturday, show construction activity at several secretive facilities built during the Cold War, including sites believed to be involved in producing plutonium cores for warheads and testing the high explosives needed to trigger nuclear detonations.

The developments come just ten days after the New START treaty between the United States and Russia expired on February 5, leaving no binding limits on strategic nuclear weapons for the first time since 1972.

item.title: Netanyahu demands Iran dismantle nuclear infrastructure in US deal
item.description:
Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu declared Sunday that any nuclear agreement between the United States and Iran must include the complete dismantling of Iran's nuclear infrastructure, not merely a pause on uranium enrichment. The demand comes ahead of a second round of US-Iran talks scheduled for Tuesday in Geneva.

Speaking at the Conference of Presidents of Major American Jewish Organizations' 51st Annual National Leadership Mission in Jerusalem, Netanyahu outlined specific conditions he conveyed to President Donald Trump during their White House meeting last week. "There shall be no enrichment capability — not stopping the enrichment process, but dismantling the equipment and the infrastructure that allows you to enrich in the first place," Netanyahu said, according to Reuters.

item.title: Iran proposes energy and mining deals ahead of Geneva talks
item.description:
Iran is seeking a nuclear agreement with the United States that would deliver economic benefits for both nations, an Iranian diplomat said Sunday, days before a second round of talks between Tehran and Washington scheduled for Tuesday in Geneva.

The discussions encompass potential business opportunities in oil and gas fields, mining investments, and even aircraft purchases, according to Hamid Ghanbari, deputy director for economic diplomacy at Iran's foreign ministry, as reported by the semi-official Fars news agency and wire service Reuters. Ghanbari argued that the 2015 nuclear pact with world powers had failed to secure American economic interests. "For the sake of an agreement's durability, it is essential that the U.S. also benefits in areas with high and quick economic returns," he said.

item.title: Gold holds above $5,000 as stronger dollar, thin holiday trading weigh
item.description:
Gold prices edged lower in early trading on Monday but held above the $5,000-per-ounce mark as a stronger dollar and profit-taking weighed on the precious metal following last week's inflation-driven rebound. Trading volumes remained thin with U.S. markets closed for Presidents Day and Chinese exchanges shut for Lunar New Year celebrations.

Spot gold slipped 0.4% to around $5,020 per ounce in early Monday trading, according to The Business Times. The pullback came after the metal recovered from mid-week lows near $4,880 to close above $5,040 on Friday, buoyed by softer-than-expected U.S. inflation data.
